summary: Valley County lookout point with no building ever constructed; a 1924 two-man post and a 1928 lightning strike; sources give 1928 or 1932 as its end.

facts.design: No lookout building; firefinder set on a post

events.note: Two men posted at the point, per a Salmon forest lookout report.
Lightning struck the lookout; the alidade melted, the firefinder glass broke and its post was shattered.
Norman Howell named as the lookout in August 1928.
Last year the site was used as a lookout point, per the 1932 record. The 1982 history puts the end in the late 1920s.

notes_for_editor: Kind is not set. A point with a firefinder on a post and no building fits the record's 'point' kind better than 'unknown'; editor to decide. Sources disagree on the end: the 1932 'last year of use' from the two Idaho lookout sites versus the late-1920s end in Bing Young's 1982 history. Both are given in the story and neither is resolved. Newspaper names differ: Idaho Fire Lookouts cites the Record-Herald for the 1928 quote and the Idaho Statesman for the staffing note; the weebly page cites the Recorder and Herald. The 1982 history places the peak on the Payette/Salmon border, while the record and weebly list only Salmon National Forest; the record's agency is left as Salmon. No source reads describe any remains, a structure or current access; the wilderness location comes from a climbing guide only.
